claims.text: The adjustment moves Akron from below the median polymer metro to above it, ON THE 56-METRO SET AND ONLY THERE. SCOPED 2026-09-01: the H1 read 'below the middle metro in dollars and above it in what it buys' with no set named, and the emphasized fragment a reader would quote alone was the half that is false elsewhere. Across all 235 metros with a disclosed polymer wage Akron sits ABOVE the middle on both measures, 92nd on the paycheck and 78th on what it buys, so the crossing is a fact about the industry's big metros and not about American metros. The denominator now travels inside the emphasized span, and both readings are asserted here so the scope cannot be dropped without the gate failing.
claims.source: derived: median nominal and median real across the 56-metro set, and Akron's rank across all 235
claims.assert: (lambda B, M, a: a['nominal'] < sorted(r['nominal'] for r in B)[len(B)//2] and a['real'] > sorted(r['real'] for r in B)[len(B)//2] and a['nominal'] > sorted(r['nominal'] for r in M)[len(M)//2] and a['real'] > sorted(r['real'] for r in M)[len(M)//2] and a['rank_nominal'] == 92 and a['rank_real'] == 78 and len(M) == 235)(D['big'], D['metros'], [r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0])

OR Akron stops sitting above the all-metro median in dollars, at which point the H1's scope clause is no longer load-bearing and can be simplified. The two halves fail separately on purpose: the first is the finding, the second is the reason the finding has to name its field.

Rewritten 2026-08-28: the annual figures were rounded to the nearest thousand, which is why $71,000 and $64,000 subtracted to $7,000 while the section head said $6,600. Every annual figure on the page is now the nearest hundred, and the rival price levels are printed so a reader can rebuild the conversions instead of taking them on trust.

The adjustment cuts Chicago's edge rather than reversing it, from $527 a week on paper to $390 in what the money buys (offer band, closer). Added 2026-09-01: the static prose stopped at the threshold, and the sentence a reader would carry away, 'a Chicago offer has to clear $71,000 to beat Akron's $64,400', reads as Chicago paying less. Only the comparator picker said otherwise, and it said it on click. Nothing load-bearing sits behind an interaction, so the print sentence now says it too.

The threshold arithmetic itself is guarded by rw-offer-arithmetic; this claim guards the sentence that says what the threshold is not.
